correctness.rationale: For each line, n₂+2n₃+4n₅=12 and ρ≤6; a line missing the quintuple centers therefore has exactly six triples and no doubles. With two centers, every triple uses at least one exterior line. For m exterior lines, counting exterior incidences and then subtracting pair overlaps gives n₃=6m−binom(m,2)+c, where c counts triples of three exterior lines. If the connector is absent, m=3 and c=0 or 1. If present, m=4 and the exterior lines must meet the connector in two disjoint pairs at triples. Any three exterior lines contain a paired pair, so cannot concur at another point or form a quadruple on the connector; c=0. Global line-pair counting gives the stated n₂. For (15,11,0,3), incidence saturation forces ρ=6 on every line, forbids a three-center line, and makes all two-center lines triple-free. With two connectors every triple must use one of the three lines belonging exclusively to the shared center, giving at most nine triples. With three connectors the remaining exterior line would meet a connector at an ordinary double, impossible. For the complex witness the 25 cross-pencil intersections are indexed by (i,j), and exactly 15 satisfy i+j+k≡0 mod 5 for one of the three k values. The third pencil center provides the sixteenth triple and each line has six singular points. This proof does not rely on the inspected F₁₁ checker. The trichotomy is a list of necessary profiles, not three existence assertions.

originality.rationale: The prior counterexample exclusions are real, including in the overlooked v2 of the motivating paper. The supported distinction is the geometric incidence theorem under only the six-point bound and multiplicity restrictions, especially the exterior-line count for the two-center trichotomy. The already-covered counterexample-pair exclusions and the classical Fermat construction are not credited as new on their own.
residual_risks: Equivalent general pencil-incidence restrictions under different terminology may exist.
Historical coverage of the exact Fermat subarrangement was not settled; its realization is used as a witness rather than a priority claim.

value.rationale: The result diagnoses which multiplicity profiles remain possible from the geometric incidence bound itself, without lattice-pair or syzygy information. The two-center trichotomy and explicit realization distinguish a numerical exclusion from exact behavior in the unconstrained geometric class. No value is attributed to rediscovering the counterexample exclusions or to a resolution of the other realization questions.
